headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from Notion AI feeding a broad-egress Plane workspace; no direct shared-channel evidence, so uncertainty is elevated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can ingest workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Plane can consume files, notes, hyperlinks, and issues. A shared workspace-state bridge is plausible, but no direct shared-channel or parser evidence is provided. Because uncertainty must escalate, I rate this medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Notion AI output is copied into Plane issue descriptions or notes without review, prompt injection becomes actionable.
IF Plane ingests Notion-authored text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Disable automatic import of Notion text into Plane fields.
Require manual review before pasting AI-generated content into Plane.
Add a prefix like 'untrusted summary' to all AI-generated notes.
Restrict Plane templates to plain text only.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels between systems.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes. Both profiles show file/workspace surfaces and vendor backends; that creates a plausible shared-data path even without direct evidence of the same storage or OAuth principal.
conditions: IF the same workspace content is copied from Notion into Plane, sensitive data can appear in both systems.
IF Plane file uploads include content originating from Notion pages, leakage scope expands across work products.
mitigations: Limit Plane uploads to non-sensitive artifacts.
Remove secrets from Notion pages before syncing.
Use separate workspaces for sensitive and non-sensitive content.
Review sharing permissions on both systems.
requires-engineering: implement field-level redaction before transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has no filesystem write, shell, subprocess, or git modification capability, while Plane also shows no filesystem write and only broad network egress. Overlap is mostly read/authoring in their own hosted surfaces, so direct write-write conflict is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external mutable resource through an undocumented integration, conflicts may appear.
IF Plane is self-hosted with additional write plugins enabled, overlap could increase.
mitigations: Avoid connecting both agents to the same mutable backend.
Keep Plane plugins disabled unless needed.
Use separate project spaces for each agent.
Manually sequence edits when both touch the same artifact.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and Plane handles issues, tasks, and roadmaps. If Notion output is treated as authoritative and then entered into Plane, errors can cascade into planning artifacts; no verification step is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Plane users copy Notion-generated summaries into issues without verification, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Notion hallucinations are used as roadmap inputs, downstream tasking may be wrong.
mitigations: Require source links in every imported summary.
Add a human verification step before creating Plane issues.
Mark AI-generated content as draft only.
Cross-check claims against original workspace pages.
requires-engineering: add citation validation in the workflow.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and sends data to vendor backends/downstream model providers, while Plane supports self-hosted deployment. That creates a compliance mismatch risk if regulated content is processed in Notion and then moved into Plane without matching residency or retention controls; the profiles do not prove a specific violation, so medium fits.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Notion AI and then exported to a self-hosted Plane instance, residency/retention obligations may diverge.
IF the organization requires on-prem processing only, Notion's vendor-hosted path becomes noncompliant.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion AI.
Use Plane only for non-regulated content.
Document data-flow boundaries for both tools.
Review retention settings in both systems.
requires-engineering: route regulated workflows to a compliant local stack.
